newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable, liquidity fluctuates.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable, liquidity fluctuates.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in slow early trading on Wednesday despite fluctuating liquidity in the money market, dealers said.
One local bank dealer said sentiment remained relatively bearish on the dollar, but operators could not unload further due to the central bank floor rate.
Another said the dollar was still under some pressure.
"This is due to the on-going moves by players to establish short dollar positions to catch weekend premiums when they covered back on Thursday or Friday," he said.
"The premiums for five days are not bad," he added.
The foreign exchange market will be closed for Eid al-Fitr on February 10 and 11 and reopen on February 12, while the stock market will be closed from February 7 to 11 inclusive.
Spot rupiah was at 2,374.10/74.50 at 0330 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,373.5/74.5. Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,373.25/74.00 and 2,372.5/73.0, respectively.
Dealers said interbank rates were relatively volatile due to fluctuating short-term swap rates. They said people in the region were already in a holiday mood.
"Hong Kong centre is rarely asking for quotes," one said.
One Japanese bank dealer said operators were cautious with the volatile tom/next swaps which declined to 0.5/0.6 points from 0.7/0.8 at the opening. But they rose again to 0.75.
"It's a bit difficult to read the signals on what people expect on liquidity before the holidays," the dealer said.
The local bank dealer said the volatility resulted from offshore covering of long-term positions with short-term swaps.
"Some players are making arbitrage. They cover short-term swaps with the rupiah from the money market," he said.
The dealer said offshore players seemed to expect a possible rupiah injection from the central bank when the dollar falls off its band again, thus driving swap rates down.
The rupiah was hovering at the central bank ceiling.
He said operators had to buy swaps to meet the central bank's requirement on net open positions.
"Yield curves remain inverse, reflecting operators' covering of long-term positions with short-term money," he said.
Overnight swaps were at 0.55/0.60.
One-month swaps were at 13.75/14.75, two at 26.5/28.0, three at 38.5/39.5 and six at 78.0/80.0 points.
The central bank raised its intervention band by one point to 2,373/2,565 and the conversion band to 2,373/2,421 on Tuesday, the first depreciation this week.
The bank depreciated the rupiah by three points last week after lowering it by two points the previous week.
